Delaware Springs Municipal Golf Course and Community, A Golfer’s Dream in the Texas Hill Country

By Texas Hill Country | October 8, 2025

 

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:42
Instaread

The game of golf has a history that some say dates back to the Roman Empire. However, most credit Scotland as the birthplace of the game we recognize today, first played on rugged terrain with wooden clubs and handmade balls. Played by millions as a leisure sport, golf has evolved into a professional sport that draws from a worldwide audience, including in the 2024 Summer Olympics.

Today’s golfer imagines living in a community of like-minded people who appreciate the mental challenge, the physical exercise, and the stunning beauty of the lush landscapes that characterize the course. It is a love for the outdoors and the fact that living in a golf course community affords the ultimate access to regularly improving one’s game that attracts many to live in areas like Delaware Springs in the stunning Texas Hill Country. 

Sometimes secrets need to be divulged, and this is undoubtedly the case with Delaware Springs Golf Course. Some call it one of Texas’s best-kept golf secrets, but everyone agrees that this beautiful 6829-yard back tees, Par 72 golf course warrants a place as one of the Hill Country’s favorite courses. Located in Burnet Texas, Delaware Springs is embraced by rolling hills and native oaks with the distinction of being one of only a few municipal courses featured in Jeff Barr’s “1001 Golf Holes You Must Play Before You Die” which is a compendium of truly great golf courses in America, Canada, Germany, England, Australia, the Philippines and other nations worldwide. 

This 18-hole championship course has been professionally designed to challenge golfers of all skill levels, featuring various water hazards and strategically placed sand traps. However, the restful and relaxing setting offers an escape from life’s stresses for a time, allowing you to focus solely on your passion for the game. Delaware Springs is also equipped with a driving range where you can sharpen your skills, as well as chipping and putting areas to improve your short game.

In addition to all the other amenities, Delaware Springs also boasts a beautifully furnished banquet facility with a large capacity, ideal for corporate retreats, banquets, business meetings, family reunions, or as a perfect wedding venue with dramatic views of the stunning Delaware Springs Golf Course. 

Life in Delaware Springs boasts dramatic sunsets overlooking the rolling hills and the oaks that grace this fantastic property, along with walking trails that wind through the golf course and the surrounding woods. 

In addition, living in Delaware Springs places you close to shopping and amenities on the square in Burnet and nearby Marble Falls, famous for its unique shops and restaurants. 

You are also within driving distance of a number of wineries that produce quality Texas wines. Relax in picturesque tasting rooms, some with restaurants and entertainment, and enjoy the famous” Hill Country Welcome” that makes this area of Texas unique.

The Highland Lakes region of Texas is one of the most desirable places to live, play, and unwind in the Hill Country. Nestled among rolling hills and sparkling blue waters, the chain of seven lakes — from Lake Buchanan to Lady Bird Lake offers a perfect blend of natural beauty and vibrant community life. Residents enjoy year-round recreation, from boating, fishing, and paddleboarding to hiking scenic trails and exploring nearby state parks.

Picturesque towns like Marble Falls, Kingsland, and Burnet provide small-town charm with modern conveniences, local wineries, farmers markets, and live music venues. With its stunning lakefront homes, breathtaking sunsets, and endless opportunities for outdoor adventure, the Highland Lakes area captures the essence of relaxed Texas living — where every day feels like a getaway.

Just minutes from Burnet and Marble Falls, the surrounding Highland Lakes area offers a perfect mix of serenity and activity. In Burnet, known as the “Bluebonnet Capital of Texas,” residents enjoy a welcoming small-town feel, historic downtown shops, and easy access to Inks Lake and Lake Buchanan for boating, camping, and fishing. The nearby Longhorn Cavern State Park and Canyon of the Eagles provide unforgettable outdoor experiences, from scenic hikes to stargazing under some of the clearest skies in Texas.

Marble Falls, on the other hand, brings a lively blend of lakefront living and modern amenities. Its charming Main Street is lined with boutique shops, art galleries, and farm-to-table restaurants, while Lake Marble Falls and Lake LBJ offer endless water recreation — from jet skiing and wakeboarding to peaceful kayaking at sunrise. With excellent schools, friendly neighborhoods, and a strong sense of community, the Burnet–Marble Falls area is an inviting destination for those seeking both adventure and a laid-back Hill Country lifestyle.

Fly Texas, Sharing the joy of non-motorized and open cockpit flying in the Highland Lakes

By Texas Hill Country | August 19, 2025

 

By Judith Shabram

If you could soar like an eagle, catching the updrafts as you view the majesty of the five stunning bodies of water that make up our Highland Lakes area, would you do it? In 1903, the Wright brothers defied existing aeronautical norms and flew the first motorized airplane from Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. Man has always had a fascination with flight, including Leonardo Da Vinci, who sketched several flying machines, convinced that one day a man would ascend into the clouds on wings of some type. In 1961, an American engineer developed and launched the first hang glider utilizing the Rogallo wing, invented by a NASA engineer in 1948. This same wing concept is used in the typical toy kite.

Hang gliding, paragliding, and powered trikes are the result of years of trial-and-error research affording man the opportunity to take wing and glide into the heavens, much like DaVinci dreamed was possible.   For some, the open-air experience is described as the ultimate adrenaline rush or thrilling. In contrast, others find the solitude peaceful and calming as you leave the fast-paced world below behind. Jeff Hunt, the owner of Fly Texas, has a mission to share the joy of flight in a special light sport aircraft. Jeff has spent over forty years gliding the skies over Texas and Mexico. His interest in aviation and flight began when he was a kid flying radio-controlled models, leading to a degree in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Texas. He worked with Tracor Aerospace for a time, but his desire was strong to dedicate himself to becoming a full-time hang gliding instructor.    Jeff is based out of Granite Shoals at the Bob Sylvester Airpark in Burnet County. Still, he spends winters in Valle de Bravo, Mexico, a world-famous destination for hang gliding enthusiasts.

With any sport, but especially flight, it is crucial to be aware of the safety guidelines and learn from a qualified instructor. Jeff is a certified flight instructor in weight-shift control, the technique used in hang gliders and the delta-wing trike. Additionally, he served for six years as a Regional Director of the national United States Hang Gliding and Paragliding Association. This nonprofit group offers programs such as Instructor Certification and Pilot Proficiency Programs. During his tenure, he organized competitions and opened new sites. Additionally, Jeff has competed in national and international cross-country and speed gliding events. Based on his years of experience and dedication to the sport, he believes it has led to a healthy flying community in Central Texas. 

Fly Texas offers two different experiences. Introduction to Power Trikes, motorcycles with wings, gets you in the air as an open cockpit pilot. A two-seater Power Trike aircraft can carry the weight of two people.   The Mile High Glide Down with the trike is just that. Power up for a breathtaking glide down and an indescribable view. Fly Texas will also train you to solo in these aircraft. A hang glider is a foot-launched non-motorized aircraft traditionally launched from enough height to get air moving across the wing to generate lift.   Since Packsaddle Mountain is no longer accessible for air sports, these trikes enable takeoffs from public and private airports, as well as smooth open fields. 

Whether for sport or recreation, non-motorized flight and open cockpit piloting continue to attract enthusiasts worldwide. These people dream of mounting on wings and climbing to the clouds to view the world from a different perspective.   Jeff Hunt and Fly Texas can be reached at 512-467-2529 and would love to answer your questions or schedule a flight. Additional information and testimonials are available at www.flytexas.com. Granite Shoals Airport 512-467-2529
